recipe.title: Dispatch existing insurance claim work without judging claims
recipe.scenario: A claims operations supervisor has already opened administrative or inspection work items. Propose assignments across teams with verified scope and available time. Do not infer severity, liability, coverage, fraud, customer priority, or settlement amount.

field.name: approved-claim-work
field.description: Opaque task ID, approved work type, externally supplied priority and due timestamps, duration, coarse operating region, and necessary role. No claim notes, claimant identifiers, diagnoses, policy attributes, or loss details.

field.name: adjuster-capacity
field.description: Opaque staff ID, administrator-verified work scope, role, permitted zones, existing reservations, available windows, and remaining task or hour limits.

field.name: handoff-dependencies
field.description: Approved predecessor tasks and the earliest confirmed handoff times. Uncompleted prerequisite tasks keep successors out of the usable queue.

field.name: travel-time-matrix
field.description: Verified rounded travel minutes between service zones and depots where travel matters; no precise claimant address is needed. Unknown travel bounds produce manual review.

field.name: dispatch-policy
field.description: Version of the approved process rules such as role/zone authorization, reserve minutes, mandatory offline review, and which tasks may be shared across teams.

field.name: proposed-task-assignments
field.description: Opaque task and proposed assignee references, approved operating region, proposed UTC work slots, and reasons. Optimize deadline coverage while observing established capacity and authorization. No claim state change.

field.name: dispatcher-review
field.description: Tasks with unknown or missing constraints or no feasible assignment; show blocked reason and requested evidence. A routing hold is not an insurance decision.
